rules.description: Only Models may call the network.
rules.check: No kite-api usage inside kite-view or kite-controller.
rules.rationale: Separation of concerns ensures predictable state flow and testability.

rules.check: Always use kite-text for text content; use kite-html only when raw HTML is explicitly intended.
rules.rationale: Strict escaping by default neutralizes Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).

rules.description: Kite never uses eval() or new Function().
rules.check: Zero eval calls anywhere in runtime, plugins, or user expressions.
rules.rationale: Permits full operation under strict Content Security Policy (CSP) environments.

rules.check: No additional window properties or prototype tampering.
rules.rationale: Prevents collision with existing host applications and backend templates.

rules.description: Every kite-* attribute must be defined in capabilities.json.
rules.check: ESLint kite/no-unknown-directive or compiler scanner check.
rules.rationale: Catches typos such as kite-fro instead of kite-for early.

rules.description: Components must communicate via props and events, not direct parent scope access.
rules.check: Ensure <kite-component> scopes do not rely on implicit parent scope leaks.

rules.description: Components must not recursively instantiate themselves infinitely.
rules.rationale: Prevents browser crash and infinite call stacks.

rules.description: Dynamic loops should not exceed comfortable limits (2,000 items max).
rules.check: kite-for loops exceeding safety threshold are truncated with warnings.

rules.description: Follow the nine-slot attribute ordering convention for readable markup.
rules.check: identity -> state -> data-in -> render -> control -> events -> lifecycle -> escape -> config
rules.rationale: Ensures visual predictability across teams and AI code generation.
